keyFindings.description: The title block's flex-basis differs between view (flex-auto, content) and edit (basis-full) below 2xl, so at 768-1279 the row re-lays out on the blur that a mousedown on any header control causes; mouseup lands on a different element and Chromium delivers the click to the common ancestor — the click on Close / Status / Priority / Approve / pin / Edit labels / Route / Subscribers / GitHub link that ends a title edit is swallowed. Reproduced with the exact classes at 1024 (Close moves (269,100)->(950,48), click target DIV) and 1279; thermo reproduced at 1200 for Close, pin, Route; control with equal basis delivers the click. Main (flex-1 min-w-[12rem] in both modes) does not have this. Fix: same basis in both modes — either `basis-full 2xl:basis-auto` unconditionally (title alone below 2xl; header unchanged at >=~900px, +1 row at 768-~900 for short titles) or a grid mirror span so the input's hypothetical width equals the text. Not by making edit basis-full at 2xl too (would move the bug to >=1536). Comment and AGENTS.md line 12 must describe the shipped rule (today both claim 'always'/'whole row' from xl, false at 2xl in both modes). Regression lock: Playwright at 1200, open title editor, mouse.down/up on Close, expect PATCH status done.

The new partial-failure unit test never waits for the check-runs query to reach status 'error' (the toHaveBeenCalledWith and the absent-pill waitFors pass immediately), so its title/state assertions can run while checks is pending — where the pre-fix `failed` logic also showed the title. Pass a QueryClient to renderIssuePage and waitFor getQueryState([github-link-checks, url, sha]).status === 'error', then assert within(link). Same push.
